dmm-2022-relay-01.title: Linear system
dmm-2022-relay-01.body:
This is problem 1.1 of the 2022 relay round; its answer $5$ is passed on as $T$ in the next problem.

Let $P_k$ be the probability of reaching $0$ or $5$ before breaking down, starting at $k$ ($P_0=P_5=1$). Then
$$P_1=\tfrac13+\tfrac13P_2,\quad P_2=\tfrac13(P_1+P_3),\quad P_3=\tfrac13(P_2+P_4),\quad P_4=\tfrac13P_3+\tfrac13.$$
By symmetry $P_1=P_4$ and $P_2=P_3$. Then $P_2=\frac13(P_1+P_2)$, so $2P_2=P_1$, and $P_1=\frac13+\frac13P_2$ gives $2P_2=\frac13+\frac13P_2$, so $P_2=\frac15$. Hence $n=5$.

**Answer: 5**

dmm-2022-relay-02.title: List the possible totals
dmm-2022-relay-02.body:
Relay problem 1.2 with $T=5$ (the answer to problem 1.1). If she slices strawberries $s$ times, then $N=3(17-s)+5s=51+2s$ for $s=0,1,\dots,17$, so $N\in\{51,53,55,\dots,85\}$ (all odd numbers from $51$ to $85$). The primes among them are $53,59,61,67,71,73,79,83$: $8$ values.

**Answer: 8**

dmm-2022-relay-03.title: Evaluate f at 1
dmm-2022-relay-03.body:
Relay problem 1.3 with $T=8$ (the answer to 1.2). Since $f(x)=(x-a)(x-b)(x-c)(x-d)(x-e)$, we have $f(1)=(1-a)(1-b)(1-c)(1-d)(1-e)=-(a-1)(b-1)(c-1)(d-1)(e-1)$ (five sign changes). Hence the required product is $-f(1)=-(1+18+19+20+21+8)=-87$.

**Answer: $-87$**

dmm-2022-relay-04.title: Bound each term
dmm-2022-relay-04.body:
Relay problem 2.1 (the start of the second chain; its answer $2$ is passed on as $T$). The square roots require $x,y\ge1$ and $xy>0$. Dividing by $xy$: $\frac{\sqrt{y-1}}y+\frac{\sqrt{x-1}}x=1$. For $t\ge1$, $\frac{\sqrt{t-1}}t\le\frac12$ by AM-GM ($2\sqrt{t-1}\le(t-1)+1=t$), with equality exactly at $t=2$. So the sum is at most $1$ with equality only when $x=y=2$. Hence $x=2$.

**Answer: 2**

dmm-2022-relay-05.title: Show a_n = n^2
dmm-2022-relay-05.body:
Relay problem 2.2 with $T=2$ (the answer to 2.1). Taking $m=n=0$ gives $2a_0=\frac12\cdot2a_0$, so $a_0=0$. Taking $n=0$: $2a_m=\frac12(a_{2m}+a_0)$, so $a_{2m}=4a_m$. Then the relation becomes $a_{m+n}+a_{m-n}=2a_m+2a_n$. With $n=1$ and $a_1=1$: $a_{m+1}=2a_m-a_{m-1}+2$, and by induction from $a_0=0$, $a_1=1$ we get $a_m=m^2$ (since $(m+1)^2=2m^2-(m-1)^2+2$). So $a_{2023}=2023^2$, whose last digit is $3^2=9$.

**Answer: 9**

dmm-2022-relay-06.title: Base 9 repunits
dmm-2022-relay-06.body:
Relay problem 2.3 with $T=9$ (the answer to 2.2). Since $a_{n+1}=9a_n+7$, in base $9$ appending the digit $7$ to $a_n$ gives $a_{n+1}$, so $a_n$ is the number written with $n$ sevens in base $9$: $a_n=7\cdot\frac{9^n-1}8$.

For $i\le88$ (larger $i$ give $a_i>a_{88}$): $a_i\mid a_{88}$ iff $\frac{9^i-1}{8}\mid\frac{9^{88}-1}8$ iff $9^i-1\mid9^{88}-1$ iff $i\mid88$. (If $88=qi+r$ with $0<r<i$, then $9^{88}-1\equiv9^r-1\pmod{9^i-1}$, which is nonzero and smaller than $9^i-1$.)

The divisors of $88=2^3\cdot11$ have sum $(1+2+4+8)(1+11)=15\cdot12=180$.

**Answer: 180**
